key_insight: Applying an inference-time, chain-of-thought–style iterative refinement loop—where a generated image is repeatedly verified and corrected against decomposed prompt constraints—substantially improves alignment for richly compositional text-to-image prompts.
problem_solved: Text-to-image models struggle to satisfy many simultaneous constraints (multiple objects, relations, and attributes) in a single prompt; existing fixes like more denoising or parallel sampling with verifiers are insufficient for complex compositional requests.
method: Decompose the input prompt into explicit sub-constraints (objects, attributes, relations) or an internal reasoning chain.
Generate an initial image with a diffusion model, run automated verifiers/constraint checks, then iteratively refine only the violating regions or aspects.
Repeat verification + localized correction until most constraints are satisfied, keeping the approach as an inference-time add-on (no model retraining required).
impact: Provides a practical, model-agnostic way to boost compositional fidelity of T2I outputs at inference time, enabling practitioners to get more reliable and controllable generations without costly retraining.

paper_title: Iterative Refinement Improves Compositional Image Generation
paper_authors: Shantanu Jaiswal, Mihir Prabhudesai, Nikash Bhardwaj, Zheyang Qin, Amir Zadeh
